messages.author: c8d66ef092f48ffe
messages.subject: Collexeme Analysis: Loading a Partial Table
parts:
Hello,
I am attempting a collexeme analysis of the abstract nouns occurring in the Det-N pattern in a few small corpora. I have two questions:

ONE: As I understand it, typically what is loaded in the txt file is a table that lists every word under analysis occurring in the corpus (in my case, singular nouns), their frequency in the collostruction, and their frequency in the corpus.

I first tried this only including the 50 most frequent words occurring in the Det-N pattern (there were 1577 total). Then I realized maybe I would not then be able to detect repulsion strengths because I didn't include all nouns, even those not occurring in the pattern. Also, maybe I would still see strong word/structure strength among those words occurring just a few times in the corpus so I should include them. Finally, and perhaps this is most important, the program prompts me for the number of Det-N occurrences in the corpus. I entered the total number of Det-N occurrences (1577), and then when uploading the table file only included those 50 mentioned earlier. Would this impact the results, since those remaining Det-N occurrences weren't to be found in the table I uploaded? I hope this question is clear, and I thank you for any advice!

TWO: Would you recommend I include all Det-N occurrences (not just those with an abstract noun) in my table? Maybe I should, since it would perhaps better reveal the degree to which the pattern "favors" abstract nouns as opposed to others (e.g. book, year, etc.).

I appreciate your time,
Brian

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Collexeme Analysis: Loading a Partial Table
parts: > ONE: As I understand it, typically what is loaded in the txt file is a table that lists every word under analysis occurring in the corpus (in my case, singular nouns), their frequency in the collostruction, and their frequency in the corpus.

> I first tried this only including the 50 most frequent words occurring in the Det-N pattern (there were 1577 total). Then I realized maybe I would not then be able to detect repulsion strengths because I didn't include all nouns, even those not occurring in the pattern.

Yes, for repulsion, you would need to include the low-frequency items
as well. Repulsion approximations for unattested items will be
provided at the bottom of the results.

> most important, the program prompts me for the number of Det-N occurrences in the corpus. I entered the total number of Det-N occurrences (1577), and then when uploading the table file only included those 50 mentioned earlier. Would this impact the results
It shouldn't impact the results for the 50 included, no.
> TWO: Would you recommend I include all Det-N occurrences (not just those with an abstract noun) in my table?

Yes.

STG
